source.quote: SMSL's own page for the D400 MK2, read 2026-11-24: « AK4191+ 1AK4499EX, tap all the potential of thechip »; « AK4499EX per channel, distortion as low as astaggering 0.00006%(-124dB) »; « New 3rd generation XMOS XU-316, PCM support up to 32bit/768kHz,DSD support to DSD512 »; « USB, optical fiber, coaxial , AES,I2S support DSD transmission, coaxialand optical fiber support DOP64 »; « Qualcomm high-end Bluetooth chip, support LDAC(24bit/96kHz),APTX/HD, sBC,AAC ».

facts.chip: « AK4191+ 1AK4499EX » with « AK4499EX per channel » - a modulator plus one converter per channel. FOURTH record in this catalogue on the AK4191+AK4499 pairing, after gustard/a26, eversolo/dmp-a8 and eversolo/dac-z10. The pairing is a house architecture across makers, and `family: akm` says none of it.

_aes_differs_from_its_sibling: Read the maker's sentence closely: « USB, optical fiber, coaxial , AES,I2S support DSD transmission, coaxialand optical fiber support DOP64 ». AES is in the first list and NOT in the DoP list, so on this device AES carries native DSD - where smsl/su-10 and smsl/su-x both put AES among the DoP-only inputs. Two models of one maker differing on one input's transport, which is exactly the kind of thing a per-input field exists to hold.
